name: short broken concrete wall stub overgrown with climbing vines: wall top seen from above, vine-covered front face
label: wasteland_ruins/vine-wall

surfaces.part: broken wall top (grey stone slab seen from above)

answer.evidence: Rows 6-11 form a light grey stone band (L about 150-160) on the wall top. It ends in a 1-row lighter front-edge line at row 12 (#bcbdc3), with a dark green shadow immediately below at row 13 in some columns. Below that, rows 13-30 form a dark green vine-covered front face of about 18 rows, with a base shadow at rows 30-31. The width profile widens from 10 to 16 over rows 5-10 as the top's back corner is cut diagonally. The wall is a single body, so no other part needs a top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a one-tile prop beside two full houses, so I judged it by tile density rather than size. It shows 13 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, and 0% near-flat coverage, the same as both references. Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline carries a tint. By eye it reads as dark green-grey beside the vines and concrete, not a black sticker line. The concrete top has a light-to-dark ramp with crack and speckle variation. The vine face uses several greens in clumps with no large flat area. It has fewer ramp steps (about 4 per material) than the roofs and walls of the references (5-6), and only 15 distinct colours in total. That is a modest palette, but the visible texture matches the reference tiles. A careful artist would accept it next to them without it looking flatter or thinner.
